selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the Second Mystery?
questions.answer: It explains that Allah’s power can deal with countless things as easily as one thing, so large and small numbers make no difference to Him.

questions.question: What three words at the start point to the reason the examples work?
questions.answer: They point to brightness, clearness, and submission.

questions.question: In the example of the sun, what does one mirror show us?
questions.answer: It shows that a single source can appear in one place without losing anything.

questions.question: What lesson comes from comparing one listener with a million listeners?
questions.answer: Reaching many does not necessarily make an action harder.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw about big and small things from the sun example?
questions.answer: It says there is no real difference for Divine power between what is large and what is small.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is needed for such broad activity to happen?
questions.answer: Divine command, Divine power, and Allah’s permission.

questions.question: How does the passage connect this example to Divine creativity?
questions.answer: It says Allah’s creative action is unlimited, so reaching many is no harder than reaching one.

questions.question: What contrast between human action and Divine action can be inferred here?
questions.answer: Humans get overwhelmed by larger numbers, but Allah does not.

questions.question: State the central lesson of the whole passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: Allah’s command and power reach countless things at once with the same ease as reaching a single thing.

questions.question: What is one respectful personal lesson a Muslim student can take from this passage?
questions.answer: We should not doubt Allah’s ability because of the greatness or number of created things, since all are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: What truth about Allah’s power is the passage trying to make clear?
questions.answer: That Allah can act in many places and upon many things at once without strain or limitation.

questions.question: What feature of the sun makes it a useful comparison here?
questions.answer: Its light can appear in many reflecting places from one source.

questions.question: Besides light, what two other effects of the sun are mentioned as reaching many reflectors?
questions.answer: Its warmth and its reflected image.

questions.question: What does the passage say a luminous being can do in relation to many places?
questions.answer: It can be present in them, observe them, or enter them.

questions.question: What does this suggest about the range of Allah’s creating activity?
questions.answer: It suggests His activity is vast and unrestricted.

questions.question: What repeated pattern do all the examples share?
questions.answer: In each case, one source relates to many receivers without added difficulty.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes this wide presence possible?
questions.answer: Divine power and Allah’s permission.

questions.question: Write the message of the passage in simple everyday words.
questions.answer: Allah can handle everything, no matter how many there are, just as easily as handling one thing.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the logic of the passage?
questions.answer: If created examples can show one source reaching many places, then Allah’s unlimited power can certainly act upon countless things with complete ease.

questions.question: What is being explained under the title “Second Mystery”?
questions.answer: A reason why Allah’s power is not burdened by multiplicity, size, or number.

questions.question: What is the first sign from the created world used to answer that question?
questions.answer: The way one sun is reflected in many places.

questions.question: What kinds of recipients of the sun’s reflection are listed?
questions.answer: Mirrors, bright surfaces, and drops of water.

questions.question: What is the second comparison taken from ordinary life?
questions.answer: One statement being heard by one person or by a huge crowd.

questions.question: How does one spoken word support the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: The same word can reach one ear or many ears, showing that one act can spread widely.
